name: Waste & Garbage Services

seo.title: Top-Rated Waste & Garbage Services in Sioux Falls, SD
seo.description: Compare waste and garbage services in Sioux Falls, SD. Find locally owned haulers with hours, contact info, reviews, and tips for choosing the right pickup plan

heroImageAlt: A blue rear-loading garbage truck parked in front of autumn trees on a clear day.
intro:
Whether you are cleaning out a basement, managing weekly household trash, or hauling away debris after a renovation, you need a reliable waste service that actually shows up on schedule. Sioux Falls winters can make collection complicated, with frozen alleys, icy driveways, and roads that change conditions overnight.

A good local waste hauler communicates clearly about holidays, weather delays, and what they will and will not take. Ask about bulk item pickup, recycling options, and whether they serve your specific neighborhood or suburb, since coverage varies and some haulers focus on certain parts of the metro.
tips: Ask whether the hauler services your specific street or alley, since not every company covers all Sioux Falls neighborhoods, Brandon, Harrisburg, or Tea.
Find out what happens to your pickup when a holiday or winter storm falls on your collection day, and whether you get notified in advance.
Ask specifically what items are accepted for recycling and whether that service is included or costs extra.
If you need a roll-off dumpster for a project, confirm the rental period, weight limits, and what materials are prohibited before you book.

faqs.q: How do I get garbage pickup at my house in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: You hire a private waste hauler, since residential trash collection in Sioux Falls is handled through private companies rather than a single city-run service. Contact a local hauler to ask about rates, cart sizes, and start dates for your address. Some neighborhoods or HOAs may already have an arrangement with a specific company, so it is worth checking with your neighbors first.

faqs.q: What can I put in my recycling bin in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Accepted materials depend on your specific hauler, so the best answer is to ask them directly for a current list. Generally, local programs accept paper, cardboard, plastic bottles, and aluminum cans, but rules around glass, plastic bags, and food containers vary. When in doubt, leaving an item out of the bin is safer than contaminating the whole load.

faqs.q: How do I dispose of large or bulky items like old furniture or appliances in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Most haulers offer bulk item pickup either as a scheduled service or for an added fee, so call your hauler first. The City of Sioux Falls also operates a household hazardous waste and large item drop-off program, so check the city website for current locations and accepted items. For large cleanouts, renting a roll-off dumpster from a local company is often the most practical option.

faqs.q: Can I rent a dumpster for a home renovation project in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Yes, several local waste companies rent roll-off dumpsters in various sizes for projects like remodels, landscaping, and estate cleanouts. Ask about the rental period, tonnage limits, and any prohibited materials such as tires, paint, or hazardous waste before you commit. Placement on a city street may require a permit from the City of Sioux Falls, so confirm that detail if you cannot fit the dumpster on your property.

faqs.q: What do waste haulers do differently in winter in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Frozen ground, icy alleys, and heavy snowfall can delay or reroute collection, and some haulers temporarily suspend alley pickup and shift to curbside service during bad weather. Reputable companies post delay notices by phone, email, or their website, so ask how a hauler communicates disruptions before you sign up. Setting your bin out the night before can help on days when weather is uncertain.

faqs.q: How do I dispose of hazardous household waste in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Items like paint, motor oil, pesticides, and batteries should not go in your regular trash or recycling bin. The City of Sioux Falls has a household hazardous waste program with designated drop-off options, and the city website lists what is accepted and when facilities are open. Your hauler can tell you what else is off-limits for curbside pickup so nothing gets rejected or causes problems at the facility.
